N1.t: Rent the model, own the data
N1.claim: Model access is becoming a commodity input. Durable value sits with whoever owns data a model can’t get elsewhere: pharma, federated pools and closed-loop data generators.
ev: Chai and Boltz build pharma-only models trained on that pharma’s own data
Lilly opens TuneLab models to 1,300+ biotechs through Benchling
Five pharmas co-train OpenFold3 without exposing their structures
N1.counter: Isomorphic’s proprietary engine more than doubles AlphaFold 3 on the hardest cases.
N1.fals: A closed-model company shows a sustained clinical-output edge using only public data.

N2.claim: The industry calls data the bottleneck, then prices the companies generating it like service shops.
ev: Tahoe at $120M (2025) against Chai at $3.8B
Tahoe‑100M became a training base for major AI labs
Virtual Cell Challenge models rarely beat naive baselines
N2.counter: Data generation is capex-heavy, and open datasets from Arc and Biohub erode exclusivity.
N2.fals: Open datasets close the performance gap with proprietary ones.

N3.claim: If pharma pays from software budgets, model companies meet Schrödinger’s ~$200M ceiling. If agents are priced against scientist headcount, today’s valuations can work.
ev: Schrödinger: $199.5M of 2025 software revenue, 10–15% ACV growth guide
Its largest value event was equity: Lilly bought Ajax for $2.3B
Edison claims six months of research per day; frontier labs ship bio models
N3.counter: AI isn’t yet cited as a cause of biotech layoffs, so labour substitution is unproven.
N3.fals: A model company reports $500M+ of software-like revenue without royalties.

N4.t: Cash lands on assets, China runs the factory
N4.stage: Consensus on assets, not on China
N4.claim: Exits flow to clinical assets. The winning structure is a platform that works as an asset factory, and China has already industrialised that.
ev: Q2 2026 set a record for VC-backed exit value, almost all asset deals
Generate was priced on its Phase 3 antibody, not its platform
Earendil raised $787M; China supplied 40% of in-licensed assets in 2025
N4.counter: BINSA could put China licensing under mandatory federal review.
N4.fals: AI platforms get acquired at platform valuations without assets.

N5.claim: Validation, regulatory credibility and biosecurity gating are becoming mandatory, with almost no capital behind them.
ev: FDA AI credibility guidance is still draft; FDA–EMA principles came in January
Bio-capable frontier models ship through trusted access
S.3741 would mandate DNA synthesis screening
N5.counter: Compliance markets are small, and CROs or the Big Four may capture them.
N5.fals: Validation stays in-house at pharma and model builders.

C1.stage: Contrarian, built with Claude, weigh accordingly
C1.claim: General-purpose AI labs become the platform winners, and specialist model companies become talent acquisitions.
ev: Anthropic paid ~$400M for a ~10-person, 8-month-old team
OpenAI made GPT‑Rosalind generally available to pharma
Both labs are Genesis Mission partners
C1.counter: Pharma trusts specialists, and general labs avoid drug liability.
C1.fals: Specialists keep winning head-to-head on design benchmarks and pharma deals.

C2.claim: Robotic science factories are a capex trap for venture money but viable when governments are the buyer.
ev: Ginkgo guides $125–150M of burn while pivoting to autonomous labs
Genesis Mission funds robotic labs across 17 national labs
XtalPi’s robotics line grew 120%+ in H1 2026
C2.counter: Lila’s reported ~$8.5B pre-money is the opposite bet.
C2.fals: A private autonomous lab reaches positive unit economics on pharma demand.

C3.claim: Foundation-model valuations repeat the 2021 platform thesis, and public markets have already re-priced that cohort.
ev: Recursion trades near $1.7B after IPO, merger and pipeline cuts
Chai at $3.8B; Lila at a reported ~$8.5B pre-money
Schrödinger retreated from independent clinical development
C3.counter: Hit rates really improved: Pfizer reported ~20% for Chai‑2.
C3.fals: The 2024–26 cohort’s first-in-human output beats the 2021 cohort’s.

china.claim: China supplied 40% of big-pharma in-licensed assets in 2025, with $135.7B of headline licensing. H1 2026 reached $92B. BINSA would add federal review.

frontier.claim: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google’s Isomorphic now sell or build directly in biology, while gating access to bio-capable models.

vcell.claim: Perturbation data, open atlases and the first virtual cell models. Benchmarks show models still struggle to beat simple baselines.

auto.claim: AI scientists plus robotic labs, from venture bets like Lila to public infrastructure like Genesis.

platform.claim: Where platforms sell software, where they own assets, and which of the two markets pays for.

carT.claim: Pharma paid $1.5B to $7B for in vivo cell therapy, including preclinical programmes, ahead of autoimmune human data.

obesity.claim: The incretin market keeps buying: Pfizer–Metsera up to $10B, China-sourced NewCos like Kailera, and AstraZeneca–CSPC.

longevity.claim: Tech-founder money funding preclinical rejuvenation at multi-billion valuations, with first human trials only now starting.

adjacent.claim: Clinician-facing AI with real revenue, priced far above most bio-AI platforms, funded by the same lead investors.
